meta.title: OrisaLang
meta.description: Orisa Language (OrisaLang) is the Dual of Ifa Language — over 20 specialized Knowledge Languages (KLs) using the Energy-based approaches of Orisa to learn all modern fields in sciences and non-sciences and build technologies.

symbols.name: Ẹyẹlé

symbols.name: Ahun

symbols.name: Ọpọlọ

symbols.name: Àràbà

symbols.name: Àkìnkanjú

symbols.name: Ẹkùn

symbols.name: Ewé Ògún

symbols.name: Ọ̀pẹ̀ Ògún
symbols.meaning: Palm — palm wine offered to Ogun, sustenance of the warrior

symbols.name: Idẹ
symbols.meaning: Brass — the sacred metal of Osun; Idẹ bracelets and rings are Osun's most important adornment, worn by devotees as a mark of her blessing and covenant with the river goddess

person.name: Ìdẹ
person.role: First High Priestess & Keeper of Osun's Sacred Brass
person.desc: Ìdẹ was the first high priestess of Osun who wore brass bracelets as a sacred covenant with the river goddess. Her unbreakable devotion and radiant beauty made her Osun's living embodiment on earth. Brass received her name and became Osun's eternal adornment forever.

symbols.name: Òòyà
symbols.meaning: Native comb — one of Osun's sacred inventions; the ivory or wooden comb that Osun created, symbolising the art of grooming, beauty, and the care of hair as a divine and sacred act

person.name: Òòyà
person.role: Osun's Master Hairdresser & Inventor of the Sacred Comb
person.desc: Òòyà was Osun's most gifted attendant — a woman of extraordinary artistry who first crafted the native comb from ivory at the river's edge. Her skill at adorning hair was unmatched across all of Yorubaland. Osun gifted the comb her name, and the sacred art of hair dressing carries Òòyà's genius to this day.

symbols.name: Iyùn
symbols.meaning: Coral beads — the sacred red coral beads of Osun; Iyùn represents beauty, royalty, and fertility. Worn by queens, priestesses, and devotees of Osun as the most precious adornment of the river

person.name: Iyùn
person.role: Royal Bead-Maker & Chief Devotee of Osun
person.desc: Iyùn was the foremost bead-maker and jeweller of Osun's sacred court — a woman whose hands shaped coral and gold into adornments of extraordinary beauty. Her work adorned queens and priestesses across the Yoruba world. Coral beads carry her name and artistry into eternity.

symbols.name: Ọmọ
symbols.meaning: Child — the greatest gift of Osun; fertility, motherhood, and the blessing of children are among Osun's supreme powers. Women journey to Osun's river to pray for the sacred gift of Ọmọ

person.name: Àṣàbí
person.role: Renowned Devotee Who Received Osun's Gift of Children
person.desc: Àṣàbí was a revered woman who prayed faithfully at Osun's sacred river for many years before receiving the divine blessing of children. Her devotion became legendary across Yorubaland and she raised eight children who became leaders in their kingdoms. Her story is still told to all who seek Osun's gift of fertility.

symbols.name: Irun Ọlọ́ṣun
symbols.meaning: Osun's sacred hair art — the intricate coiled and spiral braid patterns adorned with cowrie shells, sacred leaves, and coral; irun didi (threaded/braided hair) styled in the Ọlọ́ṣun tradition expresses divine feminine beauty, identity, and spiritual devotion to Osun

person.name: Ọlọ́ṣun Àṣà
person.role: Keeper of Osun's Sacred Hair Traditions
person.desc: Ọlọ́ṣun Àṣà was the foremost guardian of Osun's sacred hair traditions — a priestess whose intricate hairstyles mirrored the flowing patterns of Osun's river in coral, gold, and thread. Women came from across Yorubaland to receive her blessing and her art. Her hairstyling traditions are still honoured at the sacred Osun-Osogbo festival.

symbols.name: Owó Ẹyọ
symbols.meaning: Single cowrie — the Ẹyọ cowrie; a sacred and individually blessed native shell currency used in Osun's divination, sacred offerings, and consecrated trade at the river shrine

person.name: Ẹyọ
person.role: Osun's Market Queen & Sacred Cowrie Keeper
person.desc: Ẹyọ was the great market queen who oversaw all sacred trade at Osun's river market. She kept the consecrated cowrie shells that Osun blessed for commerce, ensuring each one entered circulation with divine sanction. The single sacred cowrie shell still bears her name across the Yoruba world.

symbols.name: Owó Ẹ̀rọ̀
symbols.meaning: Money cowrie — the Ẹ̀rọ̀ cowrie; the small native cowrie used in everyday Yoruba commerce and as offerings to Osun. Thousands of Ẹ̀rọ̀ cowries were counted and exchanged in the ancient Yoruba economy under Osun's blessing

person.name: Ẹ̀rọ̀
person.role: Chief of Osun's Sacred Treasury & Ancient Market
person.desc: Ẹ̀rọ̀ was the legendary chief of Osun's river treasury — the woman who first organised the counting and blessing of cowrie shells in the ancient Yoruba market economy. Her extraordinary mathematical mind and fair dealings made Osun's market the most prosperous in all of Yorubaland.

symbols.name: Aṣọ Funfun
symbols.meaning: White cloth — the sacred white garment of Osun devotees; white cloth worn in ceremony represents purity, Osun's divine light, and her covenant with the clean flowing waters of the sacred river

person.name: Funmilẹ́yọ
person.role: Weaver of Osun's Sacred White Cloth
person.desc: Funmilẹ́yọ was Osun's master weaver — a woman whose hands wove the finest white cloth from the purest threads, consecrated at the riverbank before each sacred festival. Her cloth adorned the Osun-Osogbo priestesses and was worn in the holiest ceremonies of the river goddess. The tradition of white cloth in Osun worship honours her craft and devotion.

symbols.name: Orógbó
symbols.meaning: Bitter kola — the sacred offering of Sango; bitter in taste, potent in power; the first food of fire and ritual

person.name: Orógbó
person.role: Elder Herbalist of Sango's Royal Court
person.desc: Before Orógbó became the name of bitter kola, Orógbó was a revered herbalist and elder in Sango's royal court. His mastery of sacred plants and fierce loyalty to the thunder king made him legendary. The bitter kola carries his enduring spirit.

symbols.name: Àgbò
symbols.meaning: Ram — sacred animal of Sango; symbol of virility, royal power, and fierce determination in battle

person.name: Àgbò
person.desc: Àgbò was one of Sango's mightiest warrior chiefs — fierce, relentless, and adorned in red. His unyielding strength in battle mirrored the ram's charge. The ram is offered to Sango in his eternal honour.

symbols.name: Ṣẹ́ẹ́rẹ́ Sango
symbols.meaning: Sango's sacred gourd rattle adorned with cowrie shells — the voice and call of Sango's presence in ritual

person.name: Ṣẹ́ẹ́rẹ́
person.role: Wife of Ṣango, Keeper of His Sacred Voice
person.desc: Ṣẹ́ẹ́rẹ́ was the beloved wife of Sango — a woman of extraordinary grace and spiritual power. She held the sacred rattle that summoned Sango's presence in ritual. The rattle is named after her, forever carrying her devotion to the thunder king.

symbols.name: Ọta Sango
symbols.meaning: Sango's hard stone — the neolithic thunderstone left where lightning struck the earth; Sango's bullet

person.name: Ọta
person.desc: Ọta was Sango's foremost guardian and stone-keeper — entrusted with collecting and safeguarding the sacred stones left where lightning had struck. His unbreakable loyalty and endurance gave the thunderstone its name.

symbols.name: Oṣé Sango
symbols.meaning: The double-headed battle axe of Ṣango — the royal weapon and supreme symbol of divine thunder power

person.name: Oṣé
person.role: Royal Armourer & Battle Master of Ṣango
person.desc: Oṣé was the master armourer and battle commander of Sango's royal army. He forged the legendary double-headed axe that became Sango's most sacred emblem. His extraordinary craftsmanship immortalised him in Sango's iconography forever.

symbols.name: Mọ̀nàmọ́ná
symbols.meaning: Lightning — the sacred weapon Sango hurls from the sky; swift, blinding, and all-powerful

person.name: Mọ̀nàmọ́ná
person.role: Swift Messenger & Lightning Being of Ṣango
person.desc: Mọ̀nàmọ́ná was a being of extraordinary speed and brilliance — Sango's swiftest messenger, capable of traversing the heavens in an instant. Her passage across the sky became what mortals now call lightning.

symbols.name: Àrá
symbols.meaning: Thunder — the great voice of Sango rolling across the heavens, announcing his power to all creation

person.name: Àrá
person.desc: Àrá was Sango's most powerful herald — his voice carried across vast distances, shaking the earth as it rolled. When Àrá spoke, all peoples knew Sango was near. Thunder forever carries his eternal announcement.

symbols.name: Iná
symbols.meaning: Fire — the divine element of Sango; purifying, transforming, and illuminating all it touches

person.name: Iná
person.role: Chief Priestess of Sango's Sacred Fire
person.desc: Iná was Sango's chief fire priestess — a woman of fierce beauty and burning devotion who kept the eternal flame of Sango's shrine. Her transformative spiritual power and radiant presence gave fire its Yoruba name.
